belief: Being poor means God has rejected me.
origins: In many cultures, poverty carries stigma, and that stigma can seep into our view of God. If we have been rejected by people, treated as less, or overlooked at church because of money, it is a short step to feeling that God has turned away from us too.
teaches: The psalmist says, “This poor man called out, and the LORD heard him; He saved him from all his troubles.” He prays, “I am poor and needy; may the Lord think of me. You are my helper and deliverer.” God “raises the poor from the dust and lifts the needy from the dump.” Jesus began His ministry saying the Spirit anointed Him to preach good news to the poor. Proverbs says, “The rich and the poor have this in common: The LORD is Maker of them all.” God does not reject the poor. He draws near to them.
self_statements: God has turned His back on me.
I am not important to God.
He prefers people who have more.
I am on the outside of His blessing.
I am a disappointment to Him.
Even God has given up on me.
errors: Feeling rejected and concluding that God has rejected me.
Assuming I know God’s view of me from my circumstances.
Letting people’s rejection stand for God’s.
questions: Who made me feel less because of money, and how has that colored my picture of God?
What does Scripture say about how God sees the poor?
How did Jesus treat people who had little?
What does “Maker of them all” say about my worth?
When have I sensed God near me even in a hard time?
What would change if I believed God draws near to me now?
truth: God has not rejected me. He hears the poor, helps the needy, and lifts them up. I am His, made in His image and loved. My circumstances do not change how close He is.
hw_truths: He is my helper and deliverer.
He raises the poor from the dust.
Jesus came with good news for the poor.
The Lord is Maker of us all.
log: Each day, write one moment you sensed God near, however small.
actions: Name who made you feel less.
Write the people or places and forgive them as you are able.
Look for a church or group that treats everyone as equals.
Pray honestly about rejection and ask Him to show His nearness.
prayer: Father, You hear the poor and lift the needy. When I feel rejected, remind me that I am Yours. Draw near to me, and heal the hurts that people have caused. Amen.
hw_questions: Who made me feel less because of money?
How does God see the poor?
How did Jesus treat those with little?
When have I sensed God near?
Where can I find a welcoming community?
name_example: Sarah can write: “The Lord heard this poor man and saved him, and He hears me.”
